title: The Compass of the Coral Triangle
premise: Elodie Okonkwo, a railroad engineer who inherited her grandfather's compass and a map of closed lines across the Coral Triangle, is hired to trace a decommissioned coastal railway when an upriver expedition goes silent on the radio. Drafted into the search aboard a leaking boat with a monsoon closing in, she falls in with the expedition's estranged daughter and a local pilot whose duty to his village conflicts with his growing love for her. Together they survive the storm, betrayal by the expedition's financier, and a treacherous river gorge, reaching the lost party just as glacier calving season briefly opens the high route. Elodie chooses found family over the debt that bound her, burning the map's claim to the closed lines and laying her grandfather's compass to rest at the source.
about_author: Cyrus Almeida is the pen name of a former merchant marine officer who spent a decade running supply routes through Southeast Asian archipelagos before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about maps, machines, and the people stubborn enough to follow both into trouble.

chapters.title: The Closed Lines
chapters.summary: In Elodie's POV, she arrives in a rusting port town to survey a decommissioned railway, armed only with her grandfather's brass compass and a contract debt she cannot refuse. The emotional beat is restless obligation: she measures dead track while sensing the job is a pretext for something larger.

chapters.title: Silence on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: Still Elodie's POV: the expedition upriver stops answering the radio, and the financier who hired her conscripts her engineering skills for the rescue. She meets Mara, the expedition leader's estranged daughter, who insists on coming. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Helm
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Tuan, the local pilot hired to run them upriver in a boat older than all of them. He resents outsiders but recognizes Elodie's compass as one his own father once repaired. The beat is wary mutual respect forming under the first rain bands of the monsoon.

chapters.title: The Leaking Hull
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV as the monsoon hits in earnest; the hull begins taking water faster than the bilge can manage, forcing her to improvise patches from salvaged rail plate. Mara reveals fragments of why she stopped speaking to her father. The beat is fear transmuted into competence and tentative trust.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Tuan's POV: they find the expedition's abandoned forward camp, supplies scattered, signs of a hasty move upstream — and evidence someone else followed them. Tuan suspects the financier sent a second boat. The beat is paranoia tightening like a winch cable.

chapters.title: The Financier's Shadow
chapters.summary: Mara's POV: the second boat appears, crewed by men claiming salvage rights to whatever the expedition found. A night standoff on black water ends with their fuel siphoned and a course set toward the gorge. The beat is betrayal, and Mara choosing these strangers over her own history.

chapters.title: The Gorge
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV at the climax's threshold: running rapids through a canyon with a failing engine, using her engineer's eye to read the water like stress lines in steel. They lose most of their gear but gain the high route's mouth. The beat is white-knuckle survival forging real family.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Tuan's POV as the glacier calves, opening the high route for days, not weeks. They climb toward the expedition's last coordinates while the ice groans behind them. Elodie and Tuan admit what duty each would have to break to stay together. The beat is love declared against the clock.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Climax, Mara's POV: they find the survivors — her father among them, injured but alive — cornered by the salvage crew at the route's narrowest point. A standoff resolved not by force but by Elodie revealing the map's true claim was fraudulent, collapsing the financier's legal footing. The beat is truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Compass Resting
chapters.summary: Resolution, Elodie's POV: downriver in the monsoon's aftermath, debts settled and the map burned, she lays her grandfather's compass at the river's source beside Tuan's father's mended one. Mara and her father begin again; Elodie stays, choosing the family she found. The beat is inheritance redefined as what we carry for each other.
